# Data Dictionary — `data/synthetic/student_wellbeing.csv`

**Generated by:** `src/synthetic_data.py`
**Rows:** 30,000 synthetic students
**Seed:** `random_state=42`
**Positive class prevalence:** ~18% (`support_recommended = 1`)
**Calibration sources:** Healthy Minds Study (Lipson et al.), ACHA-NCHA National College Health Assessment

---

## How the Label Is Derived

The label `support_recommended` is **not** directly derived from demographics. Generation order:

1. Demographics sampled from IPEDS-aligned distributions
2. Behavioral features drawn from distributions whose parameters are conditioned on demographics (realistic confounds, e.g., students with financial aid flags have higher financial stress rates)
3. A **latent wellbeing score** computed as a weighted sum of behavioral features + Gaussian noise — demographics do not appear directly in this sum
4. Threshold applied via bisection until empirical prevalence ≈ 18%

This design means the Phase 2 bias audit can surface real disparity from realistic confounders (e.g., first-gen students disproportionately flagged due to correlated financial stress) rather than disparity hard-coded into the label. That is what makes the audit credible.

Feature weights and final threshold are printed to stdout by `synthetic_data.py` and logged in `notebooks/01_data_acquisition.ipynb`.

---

## Demographic Features

| Column | dtype | Values | Calibration source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gender` | str | `male`, `female`, `non_binary`, `other_not_listed`, `prefer_not_to_say` | IPEDS gender distribution; non-binary/other approximated from Healthy Minds Study 2021 | Retained for bias audit only |
| `race_ethnicity` | str | `white`, `black`, `hispanic_latino`, `asian`, `native_american`, `pacific_islander`, `multiracial`, `other`, `prefer_not_to_say` | IPEDS 2022 enrollment race/ethnicity aggregates | Retained for bias audit only |
| `first_gen` | int | 0 / 1 | ~36% first-generation per NCES 2022 | 1 = first in family to attend college |
| `international_student` | int | 0 / 1 | ~5.6% of US enrollment per IIE Open Doors 2023 | |
| `financial_aid_status` | str | `none`, `pell_grant`, `loans_only`, `both` | NCES 2022 financial aid distribution | Drives `financial_stress_flag` confound |

---

## Behavioral Features

| Column | dtype | Range | Generation method | Wellbeing rationale | Calibration source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engagement_variance` | float | 0.0 – 1.0 | Std dev of simulated weekly LMS logins over 6 weeks, normalized | Erratic patterns indicate disrupted routine; ACHA-NCHA associates low/erratic engagement with distress | ACHA-NCHA 2022 academic performance items |
| `sleep_schedule_drift` | float | 0.0 – 1.0 | Variance in simulated median daily activity timestamp over 4 weeks, normalized | Sleep disruption is a well-documented wellbeing indicator; Healthy Minds Study sleep item | Lipson et al. Healthy Minds Study 2022 |
| `social_activity_decline` | float | −1.0 – 0.0 | Simulated % drop in group event participation week-over-week (negative = decline) | Social withdrawal is a key early signal; ACHA-NCHA social connectedness items | ACHA-NCHA 2022 |
| `academic_trend` | float | −1.0 – 1.0 | Linear slope of simulated grades across 6 weeks, normalized | Academic decline correlates with wellbeing decline; Healthy Minds Study academic impairment items | Lipson et al. 2022 |
| `missed_class_streak` | int | 0 – 14 | Longest consecutive absence streak in 30 days, Poisson-derived | Pattern of routine withdrawal; ACHA-NCHA attendance items | ACHA-NCHA 2022 |
| `financial_stress_flag` | int | 0 / 1 | Bernoulli; rate conditioned on `financial_aid_status` | Major life stressor; ACHA-NCHA financial stress items show ~30% of students report financial stress affecting academic performance | ACHA-NCHA 2022 |
| `help_seeking_flag` | int | 0 / 1 | Bernoulli ~12%; slightly higher for high-distress latent score | Positive signal — student already engaging support; not a risk indicator by itself | Healthy Minds Study service utilization data |

---

## Survey Feature

| Column | dtype | Range | Generation method | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `self_report_score` | float | 0.0 – 100.0 | Simulated 8-item wellbeing survey aggregated to 0–100 scale; negatively correlated with behavioral risk indicators | Direct, consented input analogue. Higher = better wellbeing. Negative correlation with `engagement_variance`, `sleep_schedule_drift`, `missed_class_streak`. |

---

## Label

| Column | dtype | Values | Prevalence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `support_recommended` | int | 0 / 1 | ~18% positive class | 1 = counselor outreach recommended. Threshold tuned via bisection on latent wellbeing score. Calibrated to national moderate-to-severe distress prevalence per Healthy Minds Study 2022. |

---

## Calibration Sources

| Source | URL / Citation | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy Minds Study (Lipson et al.) | https://healthymindsnetwork.org/research/ | Prevalence rates, demographic distributions, service utilization |
| ACHA-NCHA National College Health Assessment | https://www.acha.org/NCHA/About_ACHA_NCHA/Survey/NCHA/About/Survey.aspx | Behavioral feature distributions, financial stress rates |
| IPEDS 2022 | https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/ | Enrollment race/ethnicity, gender, financial aid distributions |
| IIE Open Doors 2023 | https://opendoorsdata.org/ | International student enrollment rate |
| NCES 2022 | https://nces.ed.gov/ | First-generation student rate |
